source_text: Μετὰ ταῦτά φησιν ἔτι πρὸς ἡμᾶς ὁ Ἰουδαῖος· ταῦτ᾿ ουν ἡμῖν ἐγκαλεῖτε, ὦ πιστότατοι, διότι τοῦτον οὐ νομίζομεν θεὸν οὐδὲ συντιθέμεθα ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐπ᾿ ἀνθρώπων ὠφελείᾳ ταῦτα ὑπέμεινεν, ἵνα καὶ ἡμεῖς κολάσεων καταφρονῶμεν; καὶ πρὸς ταῦτα δὲ φήσομεν ὅτι ἐγκαλοῦμεν Ἰουδαίοις, ἐντραφεῖσι νόμῳ καὶ προφήταις τοῖς Χριστὸν προκαταγγέλλουσιν, ἐπεὶ μήτε τὰ προσαγόμενα αὐτοῖς ὑφ᾿ ἡμῶν εἰς ἀπόδειξιν περὶ τοῦ τοῦτον εἶναι τὸν Χριστὸν λύουσιν. ἀπολογίαν ποριζόμενοι τοῦ μὴ πιστεύειν τὴν λύσιν, μήτε ὡς μὴ λύοντες πιστεύουσι τῷ προφητευθέντι, ἐναργῶς παραστήσαντι ἐν τοῖς μαθητεύσασιν αὐτῷ καὶ μετὰ τὸν χρόνον τῆς ἐνσωματώσεως ἑαυτοῦ ὅτι ἐπ᾿ ἀνθρώπων ὠφελείᾳ ταῦθ᾿ ὑπέμεινε. σκοπὸν ἔχων τῆς πρώτης ἐπιδημίας οὐχὶ κρίνειν τὰ ἀνθρώπων καὶ πρὸ τοῦ διδάξαι καὶ μαρτύρασθαι περὶ τῶν πρακτέων καὶ μὴ τοὺς μὲν πονηροὺς κολάζειν τοὺς δ᾿ ἀγαθοὺς σῴζειν. ἀλλὰ σπεῖραι παραδόξως τὸν ἑαυτοῦ λόγον καὶ μετά τινος δυνάμεως θειοτέρας παντὶ τῷ ἀνθρώπων γένει, ὡς οἱ προφῆται καὶ ταῦτα παρέστησαν. ἔτι δ᾿ ἐγκαλοῦμεν αὐτοῖς, ἐπεὶ τὴν ὑπάρχουσαν δύναμιν ἐπιδεικνυμένῳ οὐκ ἐπίστευσαν ἀλλ᾿ „ἐν Βεελζεβοὺλ, τῷ ἄρχοντι τῶν δαιμονίων.“ εἰρήκασι τοὺς δαίμονας αὐτὸν ἀποβεβληκέναι τῆς τῶν ἀνθρώπων ψυχῆς. ἐγκαλοῦμεν δ᾿ ὅτι καὶ τὸ φιλάνθρωπον αὐτοῦ, μὴ ὑπερορῶντος οὐ μόνον πόλιν ἀλλ᾿ οὐδὲ κώμην τινὰ τῆς Ἰουδαίας, ἵνα πανταχοῦ ἀπαγγείλῃ τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ, διαβάλλοντες πλάνην κατηγοροῦσιν αὐτοῦ ὡς ἀλωμένου καὶ ἀλύοντος ἐν ἀγεννεῖ σώματι· οὐ γὰρ ἀγεννὲς τὸ τοσούτους ὑπομεῖναν ὑπὲρ ὠφελείας τῶν πανταχοῦ ἀκούειν δυναμένων πόνους.
pass_a_gloss: After these the Jew says still to us: 'These things then you charge (ἐγκαλέω) us with, O most faithful (πιστότατοι), because we do not consider (νομίζω) this one god (θεός) nor agree (συντίθημι) with you that for the benefit (ὠφέλεια) of men he endured (ὑπομένω) these, so that we too might despise (καταφρονέω) punishments (κόλασις)?' And to these we shall say that we charge Jews, reared (ἐντρέφω) in law (νόμος) and prophets that announce beforehand (προκαταγγέλλω) Christ, since neither do they refute (λύω) the things brought to them by us for proof (ἀπόδειξις) that this one is the Christ, providing (πορίζω) the refutation (λύσις) as defence (ἀπολογία) for not believing, nor, as not refuting, do they believe the one prophesied, who clearly showed (παρίστημι) in those discipled (μαθητεύω) to him, also after the time of his embodiment (ἐνσωμάτωσις), that for men's benefit he endured these; having as aim (σκοπός) of the first coming (πρώτη ἐπιδημία) not to judge (κρίνω) men's affairs and, before teaching (διδάσκω) and testifying (μαρτύρομαι) about what is to be done (πρακτέα), to punish (κολάζω) the wicked (πονηρός) and save (σῴζω) the good (ἀγαθός), but to sow (σπείρω) wondrously (παραδόξως) his own word (λόγος) and with some more divine power (δύναμις θειοτέρα) in all the race of men, as the prophets also showed. Further we charge them, since him displaying (ἐπιδείκνυμι) the existing power they did not believe, but 'in Beelzebul the ruler (ἄρχων) of demons (δαιμόνια)' have said he cast out (ἀποβάλλω) the demons (δαίμονες) from men's soul. And we charge that also his love of mankind (τὸ φιλάνθρωπον), not overlooking (ὑπεροράω) not only a city but not even any village (κώμη) of Judea, so that everywhere he might announce (ἀπαγγέλλω) the kingdom (βασιλεία) of God, slandering (διαβάλλω) as vagrancy (πλάνη) they accuse him as wandering (ἀλάομαι) and roaming idly (ἀλύω) in an ignoble (ἀγεννής) body; for not ignoble is that which endured so many labours (πόνος) for the benefit of those everywhere able to hear.
pass_b_english: After this the Jew says to us further: “Is this, then, what you charge against us, most faithful ones: that we do not regard this man as a god, and do not agree with you that he endured these things for the benefit of men, so that we too might scorn punishments?”

To this too we shall say that we charge the Jews, who were brought up in the law and the prophets that announced Christ beforehand, with this: they neither refute the proofs we bring them that this man is the Christ, and so make the refutation their defence for not believing; nor, since they cannot refute them, do they believe in the one who was foretold. He showed plainly, in those who became his disciples, even after the time when he was in the body, that he endured these things for the benefit of men. The aim of his first coming was not to judge human affairs and, before teaching and bearing witness about what must be done, to punish the wicked and save the good. It was rather to sow his own word in a wonderful way, and with a power more divine, in the whole human race, as the prophets had also shown.

We also charge them because, when he displayed the power that was his, they did not believe him, but said that he cast the demons out of human souls “by Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons” (Matthew 12:24; Luke 11:15). And we charge them that they slander even his love for humanity. He did not overlook a single city, nor even a single village, of Judea, so that he might proclaim the kingdom of God everywhere (Matthew 9:35; Luke 8:1); yet they slander this as vagrancy, and accuse him of wandering and roaming about in an ignoble body. But a body that endured so many labours for the benefit of those everywhere who could hear is not ignoble.

choices.term: ἀπολογίαν ποριζόμενοι τοῦ μὴ πιστεύειν τὴν λύσιν
choices.why: ἀπολογίαν ποριζόμενοι τοῦ μὴ πιστεύειν τὴν λύσιν: 'offering the refutation as their defence' changed to 'and so make the refutation their defence' (the refutation is what they fail to supply, so the clause must not read as something they actually do)
Removed causal 'For' before 'he showed plainly': the Greek is a relative participle (παραστήσαντι), not a reason clause

choices.term: μὴ ὑπερορῶντος οὐ μόνον πόλιν ἀλλ᾿ οὐδὲ κώμην
choices.why: μὴ ὑπερορῶντος οὐ μόνον πόλιν ἀλλ᾿ οὐδὲ κώμην: stiff 'passed over not only no city, but not even any village' changed to 'did not overlook a single city, nor even a single village'
Speaker check: the Jew's question in quotation marks; θεόν lower case in his mouth. Checked: Matthew 12:24 and Luke 11:15 (Beelzebul wording), Matthew 9:35 and Luke 8:1 (cities and villages, kingdom)

translator_notes: ὦ πιστότατοι is ironic (‘you most faithful/credulous’); rendered ‘most faithful ones’ to keep the play on πίστις. θεόν in the Jew’s mouth is lower case (‘a god’), as he denies Jesus’ divinity. The transmitted καὶ μὴ before τοὺς μὲν πονηροὺς κολάζειν is awkward; read as part of the list of what the first coming was not for, which the μὲν ... δέ and the ἀλλά clause require. μετὰ τὸν χρόνον τῆς ἐνσωματώσεως: ‘after the time when he was in the body’, i.e. after his earthly life. ἐν Βεελζεβούλ, τῷ ἄρχοντι τῶν δαιμονίων matches Matthew 12:24 and Luke 11:15 (Mark 3:22 has a slightly different wording). The tour of cities and villages is an allusion (Matthew 9:35; Luke 8:1), cited inline. ‘Wandering and roaming about’ echoes Celsus’s charge of a vagrant life; no quotation marks because Origen paraphrases.
